Irinotecan and temozolomideNational Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) 00504

Record each cycle separately. Each medicine has its own symptom table. Mark the worst symptoms since your last review, when they occurred and what they stopped you doing. Overlapping symptoms can be recorded under more than one medicine; you do not have to identify the cause.

These are patient-language severity prompts, not a validated questionnaire or a formal Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading tool. Your team assigns the clinical grade. Serious symptoms override the columns: call without waiting to decide a severity level.
Use a new record sheet for each cycle or review. Copy or print another sheet when needed; the number of sheets does not prescribe the length of treatment.

Irinotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in handling deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Cancer-cell division is disrupted. Blood and bowel cells are also affected. Early infusion-related bowel symptoms and later diarrhoea need different treatment plans.

What to watch forTell staff about cramping, sweating, runny eyes/nose or diarrhoea during or soon after infusion. Later watery stools require the prescribed diarrhoea plan and immediate oncology contact. Fever, dizziness, reduced urine, severe abdominal pain or inability to drink needs urgent assessment.

The body converts temozolomide into an active substance that damages deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, interrupting cell division. Although taken as capsules, it can cause serious blood, liver and infection problems and requires the prescribed checks.

What to watch forReport fever, new cough or breathlessness, unusual bleeding, jaundice, severe rash or persistent vomiting urgently. Take capsules exactly as prescribed; do not replace a dose after vomiting. Follow the infection-prevention prescription and report any missed doses to the team.

If you vomit after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose.

Prospective interim trial evidence and retrospective studies show activity in some relapsed Ewing sarcomas. In the rEECur comparison, the irinotecan/temozolomide arm was less effective than the other then-open arms and was closed.
